title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Exercise Effects in Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity
author: Juliene Gonçalves Costa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b4x6qxre
materials: Languages: English, Portuguese, Italian, French and Spanish;

steps.title: Search for Eligible Studies
steps.instruction: Search the PUBMED, EMBASE, CINAHL, Sportsdiscuss, and Prospero electronic databases for intervention studies published from 2000 onwards.

steps.title: Screen Studies Based on Eligibility Criteria
steps.instruction: Evaluate studies based on the following criteria: population (adults >18y, both sexes, with two or more health conditions, at least one being cardiometabolic such as hypertension, heart failure, coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, diabetes, or obesity), intervention (chronic physical exercise/activity of any modality, with or without co-interventions like diet or behavior change therapy), control (not limited), outcomes (6-minute walking test, VO2peak, body weight, body mass index, waist circumference, and quality of life), and languages (English, Portuguese, Italian, French, and Spanish).

steps.title: Screen and Extract Study Records
steps.instruction: Perform screening, eligibility assessment, and data extraction in duplicate using two independent reviewers, resolving disagreements via a third reviewer.

substeps.instruction: Organize studies in the Mendeley reference manager and a data extraction spreadsheet.
Use WebPlotDigitalizer to extract numerical data from graphs or figures if clear numerical representation is missing.

Extract outcome values (BMI, body weight, waist circumference), population characteristics (sex, exercise training level, average age, health status), and exercise characteristics (duration, modality, intensity, total volume, and presence of other interventions).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Appraise the methodological quality and risk of bias of included studies independently using two reviewers, resolving disagreements through discussion among all authors.

substeps.instruction: Use the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal tool for Randomized Controlled Trials.

Answer 13 questions to judge bias as 'Yes', 'No', 'Uncertain', or 'n/a' regarding randomization, blinding, group similarities, care type, pre/post-intervention measures, follow-up procedures, outcome measures, result reliability, and statistical analysis adequacy.
Describe any reported conflicts of interest.

steps.title: Perform Data Synthesis and Quantitative Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using the R programming language with the 'meta' and 'metafor' supplements.

substeps.instruction: Analyze data based on weighted or standardized mean differences.
Calculate and present Kendall's tau and I² consistency measures.
Generate a forest plot for summary meta-analysis values.
Perform subgroup analysis based on intervention duration (weeks) and volume (total), if sufficient studies exist.

Conduct sensitivity analysis for exercise modality (aerobic, resistance, combined, yoga, tai chi), type of intervention (physical exercise or physical activity), association type (exercise only or exercise with diet/counseling), and gender.
Identify outliers using the 'externally standardized residuals' method and influential points using Difference in Fits (DFFITS), Covariance Ratio, and Cook’s distance methods.
Analyze publication bias using a funnel plot and asymmetry hypothesis tests (fail-safe n, Egger, and Beggs).

description: Background Worldwide, more than 60% of the adult population has at least one chronic disease and 20% to 30% are affected by two or more chronic diseases, with cardiometabolic diseases being the most frequent and the main causes of death in the world. People with multiple chronic diseases have a greater chance of hospitalization, longer hospital stay, worse general health status, worse physical and mental function, and lower functional capacity, with an average risk of 50% functional decline with each additional condition [1,2]. Among the non-pharmacological interventions with proven beneficial effects, the practice of physical exercise stands out as an adjuvant treatment and plays an important role in the prevention of cardiometabolic multimorbidity. The practice of a healthier lifestyle, including regular physical activity, was associated with up to 7.6 more years of life for women, improving the general health status of the individual, especially those with multimorbidity. While lower levels of physical activity were associated with increased prevalence of multimorbidity in women aged 16 to 24 years [3,4]. The beneficial effects of physical exercise interventions were demonstrated in the review by Bricca et al, on quality of life outcomes, functional capacity and adverse effects in a population with multimorbidity [5]. However, new approaches to interventions with a multimorbid population are recommended, such as the use of disease patterns to limit the multiple combinations, in addition to interventions aimed at different aspects of the patient, in a multidirectional care [6,7]. Thus, the objective of the review proposed here is to answer the following question: what are the effects of physical exercise and physical activity on body composition, physical capacity and quality of life in individuals with cardiometabolic multimorbidity?
